- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; correct by adding 10–30% to forecasted values for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and prices are trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 15–25% for the next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently over-estimates short-term (1–3 day) price movements after sentiment shifts; apply a 2–5 day lag correction by smoothing out sharp spikes.
- After a large spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 10–20% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and history shows mean-reversion, model tends to over-forecast; apply a mean-reversion bias correction: subtract 5–15% from forecast for 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model under-estimates long-term price trends when sentiment is positive; increase forecast by 10–20% for the first 10 days of the horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by positive, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add a “reversal buffer” of +5–10% to forecast for the 5–7 day window after sentiment turns positive.
